# generator-shortcuts — exact answer

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed generator emits such cases.

## The rival: fill only isolated pluses

My strongest practical candidate is `isolated_plus`: fill an empty center only when its four cardinal neighbors are blue **and all four diagonal neighbors are zero**. This is a small extra condition that matches the sparse visual appearance of the canonical examples and the original generator. The intended rule does not inspect diagonals. “Strongest” is an assessment of plausibility here, not a ranking proved against every imaginable hypothesis.

The executable rival fits **all 3/3 labeled canonical pairs**: both training demonstrations and the labeled canonical test. That result is recorded under `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS.isolated_plus` in `checks/local-contract-verified.json` and the corresponding namespaced entry in `checks/lesson-census-verified.json`. Horizontal-pair alone is a weaker all-canonical claim: it fits 2/3 and is not presented as a shortcut fitting every labeled pair.

## Exact counterexample

Input: 3 rows × 3 columns. Output: 3 rows × 3 columns.

```json
{
  "input": [[0,1,0],[1,0,1],[0,1,1]],
  "actual_racket_output": [[0,1,0],[1,8,1],[0,1,1]],
  "isolated_plus_output": [[0,1,0],[1,0,1],[0,1,1]]
}
```

The four cardinal neighbors of the center `(1,1)` are all `1`, the center is `0`, and the lower-right diagonal is `1`. The authority changes the center to `8`. The rival incorrectly leaves it zero. The other eight cells are preserved. The input passes the repaired task validator.

This is case 171 in the binary enumeration of the returned probe. Its minimality is scoped to that enumerated corpus: minimum area, then number of nonzero cells, then row-major values. It is a compact constructive witness, not a claim of global proof by minimality.

## How the output was checked

Run from the outer issued packet root after applying the patch:

```bash
python3 review.py run python3 generators/80f776fb3ce5/workspace/probe_local_contract.py --out ../checks/local-contract-verified.json
```

Use a new output filename when rerunning: the tool refuses to overwrite prior evidence. The wrapper executes inside `WORK/repo`. The probe calls the supported `arcpuzzles.Catalog.apply` API in batches of at most 64 and retains its authority receipts, input/output hashes and canonical/source identities. It compares actual Racket outputs with an independent Python original-input predicate. Across all 512 binary neighborhoods and 56 palette/occupied-center cases, the predicate disagreed with Racket on **0/568** cases; the isolated-plus rival was refuted on **23/568** local cases. Its particular witness and provenance are also saved in the task's `counterexamples/isolated_plus_minimal.json`.

All final results bind generator SHA-256 `a30c04fd21088af1a4f89745861eb389b2745ded0ccbe199c9b40774294b10fb` and canonical rule hash `b2e92ad6e68e`. The normalized full rule SHA-256 is `b2e92ad6e68e68cbe166833f46c7406360bc66f52b5b82b88e4d5816333e1edc`. No authority source was changed.

## Does the repaired generator emit this distinction?

**Yes, as part of larger contrast scenes.** The exact 3×3 grid above is a local diagnostic and is not emitted as a whole input, because advertised generated dimensions start at 6. Default odd-index contrast scenes contain valid centers with diagonal clutter, together with a clean positive and several close negatives. The first cluttered target permits one, two, three or four blue diagonal cells; the retained regression covers all those counts plus zero at a clean target.

`counterexamples/isolated_plus_generated.json` retains a complete, actually generated final-source input, its Racket output, rival output and census seed/sample provenance: easy difficulty, seed `900844272`, accepted sample index `1`, no overrides, the second training pair of census lesson 0. Input: 14 rows × 12 columns. Output: 14 rows × 12 columns. Racket changes four centers; the isolated-plus rival changes only the one with zero diagonal clutter. Its source is `checks/lesson-census-verified.json`, which retains every materialized lesson and the actual accepted indices. This separate example establishes emitted support; validator acceptance of the 3×3 alone would not.

The final semantic input census observed the diagonal-clutter witness in **298/600** draws. Complete default lessons use **3 demonstrations + 1 query** and a period-2 clean/contrast schedule, so every four-pair window has two contrast scenes. The larger production census found no declared-rival ambiguity in **300/300 lessons** or **1,200/1,200 hold-one-pair-out rotations**; the required semantic gate independently passed **12 lessons and 48 rotations**. There were 1,133 unique input grids in the larger census, rather than 1,200 independent inputs.

The guarantee is scoped to default lesson assembly and the ten distinct implemented rivals. Compact overrides can remove the contrast profile; arbitrary clutter, more than four targets, no-op inputs and other hypotheses are not certified. The separate count-capped-at-three rival also fits all canonical pairs, cannot be refuted by a single 3×3 local input, and is addressed by the default four-target scenes and its own executable witness.
